To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

WISER: - is an unsupervised semantic search engine for finding experts in the academia; - jointly combines classical language modelling techniques with the Wikipedia Knowledge graph; - models author's expertise with a small semantic graph drawn from Wikipedia; - achieves state of the art results in the expert finding task; - can be used for indexing and profiling a whole university research community.

(i) we have developed an expert finding system that combines classical language modelling techniques with the use of the Wikipedia Knowledge Graph via entity linking and that (ii) this system outperforms the other competitors on a standard dataset, and that (iii) the application of this system to the whole research community of our University has proved to be useful for technology transfer.

(i) we propose a new, unsupervised, semantic approach to expert finding, which combines classical language modeling with the Wikipedia Knowledge graph, (ii) we show that our approach achieves better performance than the other competitors on a standard dataset, and (iii) we describe a successful application of our approach for technology transfer in the University of PISA.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a semantic search engine for academic expert finding, which can be used to identify and profile the research community of the University of PISA, and to support technology transfer activities in our University.

the design and development of a new semantic search tool for expert finding in the academic community, which combines the advantages of traditional language models with the power of the knowledge graph.

the following aspects: 1) the design and development of WISER, an unsupervised expert finder for academia; 2) the design and evaluation of a new profiling technique for academic authors; 3) the design and implementation of a large-scale application of our system to the University of PISA; 4) the evaluation of WISER over a large scale benchmark dataset.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
WISER represents a significant step forward in expert finding in academia.
our work is a step forward in the field, and that we are confident that our system will become a useful tool for the University of PISA and for the Italian scientific community.
WISER represents a new paradigm in the area of expert finding and, more in general, of semantic search engines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to retrieve the best expert in the field of the query topic, even in the case of rare and specific topics.
WISER is a semantic search engine that combines the best of two worlds: the power of classical text-based search engines with the power of the Knowledge Graphs.
WISER is a semantic search engine for academia that is able to provide a list of experts for any research topic, and that can be easily applied to the entire research community of a University.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the semantic representation of the research community, via the use of a graph of entities and their semantic relatedness, can provide a powerful tool for expert finding in the academia.

the use of semantic technologies, in the form of a proper semantic representation and search engine, is a powerful tool for expert finding in the academia, which is a crucial task for technology transfer and innovation.
the use of semantic knowledge bases and entity linking can improve the quality of the results in expert finding systems.
